title: And Must This Body Die
description: And Must This Body Die in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 110, headed “Triumph over death in hope of the resurrection”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: And must this bo-dy die? This mor-tal frame de-cay? And must these ac-tive limbs of mine Lie moul-dering in the clay?

lines: And must these active limbs of mine
Looks down, and watches all my dust,
Till he shall bid it rise.
And every shape and every face
We would adore his grace below,
Till tunes of nobler sound we raise

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
